paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Yunnan, made in 2024. Red tea is what English calls black tea. The Chinese name follows the colour of the cup, and the tea is fully oxidised: the rolled leaf is left until it turns from green to reddish brown. In Yunnan the style is [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition). It [began in late 1938](dian-hong:history), when the war cut China off from its eastern tea regions and Feng Shaoqiu made a trial batch at Shunning, now Fengqing, from the province's large leaf.
At two years this leaf still sits within the window the trade favours for the style, its first one to three years. [Dian Hong is kept](dian-hong:ageing) for freshness rather than for age.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
